title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is attaching canonical metrics to conformal surfaces X, possibly with boundary. He does this through the conformal double X^~ = 𝔛, which carries an anticonformal involution σ whose fixed set is the image of ∂X. The previous page shows the following. If 𝔛 carries a canonical metric that is invariant under conformal automorphisms (and, he says, under anti-automorphisms, with the explicit exception 𝔛 ≅ ℂ), then that metric descends to X and makes ∂X geodesic. In the hyperbolic case this is the hyperbolic metric of the double.

This page first concludes that the descent procedure gives a well-defined metric once it is supplemented by the prescription of choosing a 'distinguished' metric on X^σ that is σ-stable. He then turns to the 'only new cases': X connected with ∂X ≠ ∅. Equivalently, 𝔛 is connected and carries an antiinvolution σ with 𝔛^σ ≠ ∅. He lists the cases that are problematic for the existence of a canonical metric on X.

Case (a), 𝔛 ≅ ℂ:
- Every anticonformal automorphism of ℂ has the form z ↦ a z̄ + b, with a ∈ ℂ* and b ∈ ℂ.
- For an antiinvolution with fixed points, one may assume 0 is fixed, so b = 0 and σz = a z̄.
- Then σ² = id forces a ā = 1, i.e. a ∈ U (the unit circle).
- Writing a = α² with α ∈ U gives σz = α² z̄ = (α/ᾱ) z̄. This is the orthogonal reflection in the line α·ℝ, and ℂ^σ = α·ℝ.

On the next page he notes that all antiinvolutions of ℂ have fixed points: they are the reflections in real lines, not necessarily through 0. Hence X is a closed half-plane, and the Euclidean metrics invariant under σ form a 'line' of metrics (a one-parameter family up to scaling). Aut of the closed upper half-plane is identified with the real affine group. The purpose is to classify the exceptional (non-hyperbolic) bordered cases in which no canonical metric exists, only a family up to constant.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor gap: the reduction to b = 0 presupposes a fixed point. Grothendieck notes on the next page that this is automatic. From σ² = id one gets |a| = 1 and a b̄ + b = 0, so with a = α², b/α is purely imaginary; the fixed-point equation is then solvable, and the fixed set is a line.

ideas.what: Canonical metric on a bordered Riemann surface obtained by descending the canonical (uniformizing) metric of its Schottky double; the boundary becomes geodesic.
ideas.modern_name: Schottky double / uniformization of bordered surfaces, hyperbolic metric with geodesic boundary
ideas.where_published: Perhaps alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (discussion of surfaces with boundary / 'surgery' of conformal surfaces); not developed there

ideas.what: Classification of antiinvolutions of ℂ as reflections in real lines; the quotient is a closed half-plane.
ideas.modern_name: Real structures on the affine line / anticonformal involutions of ℂ

deep.surprise_reason: Routine elementary computation (antiinvolutions of ℂ) inside a case analysis of exceptional, non-hyperbolic bordered surfaces for canonical metrics. It is correct and classical, with nothing new.
transcription_corrections: 'par la présomption que l'on' should read 'par la prescription que l'on' (matches 'prescription' on the previous page).
'compactés [?] i.e.' is more likely 'connexes, i.e.' or a similar qualifier, not 'compactés'.
'si on prend une antiinvolution : pts fixes' likely reads 'si on prend une antiinvolution à pts fixes'.
'(qui assure [?] σ²=id)' plausibly '(ce qui assure σ² = id)'.
'{+symétrie par r. à la droite α.ℝ+}' is a marginal note: 'symétrie par rapport à la droite α·ℝ'.
Next page: 'les [?] triangulations[?] de ℂ' should read 'les antiinvolutions de ℂ'.
